reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis is scientifically sound: V is known to form grain-boundary precipitates in some alloys, and grain-boundary engineering can improve toughness without drastically altering bulk phase transitions, though the specific claim of <5% caloric change in this complex MM'X HEA is optimistic and lacks direct supporting evidence.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and decisive: it specifies quantitative thresholds (≥30% strength increase, <5% caloric deviation) and microstructural confirmation via TEM, which would directly falsify the hypothesis if not met.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is useful and worth testing because it proposes a specific, rare-earth-free, single-intervention route to simultaneously improve mechanical integrity and preserve caloric performance, directly addressing the core limitation of the material.
